newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says favors tax break for struggling D.C.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says favors tax break for struggling D.C.

text.p: President Clinton said he favored a tax break to help the financially struggling District of Columbia.
"I think there needs to be an economic incentive in the form of tax relief," Clinton told reporters at a press briefing.
He said he had not yet read a D.C. flat tax bill introduced this morning by the city's delegate to the U.S. Congress, Eleanor Holmes Norton.
Clinton said he agrees with her on the general point of the bill, which is that additional tax incentives are needed for increased investment in the city.

"I have not seen what Norton released today," Clinton said. "The last time this came up the folks at Treasury (Department) and the Office of Management and Budget thought the proposal was more costly than we can afford," he added. Norton first introduced the bill last year, but House committeesdid not vote on it.
Clinton said he intends to make a tax-related proposal for D.C., "and I think it will be a significant incentive for people to invest in D.C. and grow the economy here," he said.
"I think that's a very important component. I agree with her on her general point," he said of Norton's tax-relief bill. "I just have to see specifics before I can make a commitment," he said.
Norton's bill would scrap the current federal tax schedule for D.C. residents, which has rates as high as nearly 40 percent.
It would set a federal income tax ceiling for D.C. residents at 15 percent and cut capital gains taxes on investments by D.C. residents in the city.
